title: The 12-bar blues
summary: Twelve chords, three of them different: the backbone of blues and rock and roll.

steps.title: 12-bar blues
steps.body:
The **12-bar blues** is a progression of twelve chords using only I, IV and V: I I I I, IV IV I I, V IV I I. In C major that is four of C, two of F, two of C, then G, F, C, C.

**Why it matters:** Blues, rock and roll and lots of funk are built on it. Band mates can jam on it with no rehearsal: someone just says "blues in G".

steps.title: The blues in G
steps.body: I is G, IV is C and V is D.

items.prompt: Play the 12-bar blues in C: I–I–I–I–IV–IV–I–I–V–IV–I–I.
In C major, which chord is the IV?

steps.title: Jam it
steps.body: Play the 12-bar blues in C with your left hand on the roots, and make up a tune with your right hand on C, E♭, F, G and B♭.

items.prompt: Play the 12-bar blues in G: I–I–I–I–IV–IV–I–I–V–IV–I–I.
In A major, which chord is the V?
